clue.text: Be up in time for discussion

indicators.note: the reversed pair of letters is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word Be is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get out of bed promptly for a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be up' reads as getting out of bed, but 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal argument over an issue is a synonym for discussion.

clue.text: Impact he made in strong terms

indicators.note: made here means fashioned into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A man's forceful words had an impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals rearranging the letters of IMPACT HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceful and stressed speech is said to be put in strong terms; the adjective describes such forceful expression.

clue.text: Quietly managed church dance

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
to run something is to manage it
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church dance was organised without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper or step about in a lively, high-spirited way is a kind of dancing.

clue.text: No way to get wealthy — you'll just get the bird

parts.note: O, a nought, stands for nothing or no
ST is short for street, a way
rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: A cynic warns that there is no route to riches and you will just be mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' is slang for being booed or jeered, which misdirects from the literal bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African runner is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Bill comes up with new coil of fabric

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of coil

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An invoice arrives along with a fresh roll of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns AC into CA; 'new' rearranges COIL into LICO.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain woven cotton cloth is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Disciple has to stick to holy writ

parts.note: to adhere is to stick
NT is the New Testament, part of holy writ

explanation.surface: A follower must keep faithfully to scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or teacher is the same as a disciple.

clue.text: Many seem disconcerted with increase for entrance

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

indicators.note: disconcerted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the anagram fodder
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: Lots of people look flustered by a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway noun but is the verb, to enthral; 'disconcerted' jumbles the second word to give ESME.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance is to captivate or hypnotise someone, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Robust half of comedy duo

definitions.meaning: Oliver, partner of Stan Laurel in the film comedy pair

explanation.definitionFit: Tough and able to endure is a synonym of robust; Oliver of Laurel and Hardy is the comedy duo's other half.

clue.text: Girl reaches across ravine to get plant

indicators.note: the girl's name spans either side of the ravine word, enclosing it

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a chine is a deep narrow ravine, in southern England especially

explanation.surface: A girl stretches over a gorge to reach a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHINE is a steep ravine on the Isle of Wight or Dorset coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in the industrial sense means the machinery and equipment of a works.

clue.text: Ruled out, showing signs of age

definitions.meaning: marked out with ruled lines, as writing paper is
wrinkled, as an ageing face is

explanation.definitionFit: Paper ruled out has lines on it; a wrinkled face has lines, a sign of ageing.

clue.text: Short of ammunition

parts.note: read not as lacking bullets but as the shortened, clipped form of the word ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: The informal clipped word for bullets and shells is a shortening of the full word ammunition.

clue.text: A fine state to be in

definitions.text: A fine state to be in

parts.words: A fine state to be in
parts.note: evokes the idiom of being in fine condition, the word that follows 'in fine' in the phrase

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means condition or shape, used almost only in the idiom of being in fine form.

clue.text: Calm artfully created

definitions.meaning: written or put together, as music or verse is

explanation.definitionFit: Collected and serene matches calm; music written by a composer is likewise created with art.

clue.text: Cool beat from the backing group

parts.note: to fan is to cool
to club is to beat

explanation.surface: A band's backing singers lay down a cool beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing group' suggests musicians; here it means supporters who back a star.
explanation.definitionFit: An organised body of admirers supports, or backs, a celebrity or team.

clue.text: Tell everyone girl's gained weight

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name; the 's stands for 'has'
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Gossip about a woman putting on weight is spread to all.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim publicly is to make something known to everyone.

clue.text: Surgeon's inner compulsion

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word are the ones wanted

explanation.surface: A doctor feels a deep drive to operate.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong desire or impulse is a near synonym for a compulsion.

clue.text: Stays in company with the right cliques

parts.note: sets are cliques or circles of people

explanation.surface: Someone remains with a firm that has the correct social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb; it is a noun, the old word for stiffened undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is an old name for boned, stiffened underwear worn to shape the waist.

clue.text: Contradictory orders to the yachtsman for more canvas

parts.note: a sailor might be told both to remain put and to set off, two commands that clash
a sailor might be told both to remain put and to set off, two commands that clash

explanation.surface: A sailor receives conflicting commands about extra sailcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay!' and 'Sail!' contradict each other, and together name a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: This triangular sail set on a stay adds extra sail area, more canvas.

clue.text: A London club magazine

definitions.meaning: a store of weapons and ammunition

explanation.definitionFit: A weapons depot is a military magazine; the Gunners are a London football club of the same name.

clue.text: Risk death with passion

parts.note: death is the end of life
anger is a passion, a strong emotion

explanation.surface: A hot temper risks someone's death.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in peril or jeopardy is to risk something, in the verb sense.

clue.text: It's behind an article getting serious

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
stern means serious or severe

explanation.surface: Something at the back becomes grave.
explanation.walkthrough: In nautical use this word means at or towards the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical adverb means towards the rear or back, which is behind.

clue.text: Composer of number in brash arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement re-orders things, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number
part of the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A musical work is set in a loud, showy style.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes, the German Romantic, is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Violin piece needs quartet to play it

definitions.meaning: the part of a violin supporting the strings
a card game for four players

explanation.definitionFit: The violin's string support is one sense; the four-handed card game is the other.

clue.text: Everybody satisfied about powerful striker

indicators.note: the word for satisfied goes about, around, the word for everybody

parts.note: a need that is met is satisfied
all means everybody

explanation.surface: The whole crowd is pleased with a strong centre-forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer; it is a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy-headed hammer is a tool for striking hard.

clue.text: Leaves with all debts settled

explanation.definitionFit: To leave or abandon is one sense; being even, with nothing owed, is the other.

clue.text: Revised plan in use for land project

indicators.note: a revised plan is altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A development plan currently in use has been redrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land project' suggests development; 'project' here means jut out.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of land that projects into the sea is literally a land projection.

clue.text: Some players make it, others read it

definitions.meaning: sportsmen run up a tally of points or runs
musicians read the written music of a composition

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both points tallied in a game and written orchestral music.

clue.text: Continued to argue terms — lawyers benefited

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
gained means benefited

explanation.definitionFit: To haggle over the terms of a deal is to keep arguing terms.
